title: Deterministic shard affinity for console telemetry streamer
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem statement: our real-time console metrics pipeline shows intermittent tail-latency spikes and elevated processing lag during consumer group rebalances and tenant churn. Root-cause analysis points to frequent shard reassignment and cold-starts of per-partition state (KV caches, prefix caches) which causes 200-600ms processing slow-paths and transient backlog for high-cardinality tenants.

Goal: introduce a deterministic shard affinity and graceful handoff path for the console telemetry streamer such that partition ownership changes are minimized, cold starts are handled in the background, and per-partition processing latency variance is reduced. The change should be togglable by cluster and support gradual rollout.

Scope: implement an affinity coordinator (lightweight service/leader) that issues deterministic assignments using consistent hashing + virtual nodes; update consumer clients to use lease-backed sticky ownership with passive handoff; implement a background catch-up worker for newly-assigned partitions that warms KV/prefix caches before accepting live traffic; add metrics and fatal-path alerts for rebalance counts, handoff duration, and percent of records processed on cold-path.

Out of scope: full rewrite of the ingestion protocol, migration of historical batched pipelines, or changes to storage sinks beyond idempotent write guarantees already in place.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline-level 99th percentile per-record processing latency for console metrics reduces by >= 35% during tenant churn (measured on staging traffic replay)
Rebalance frequency (number of partition ownership changes per hour) drops by >= 60% for stable clusters in 48h canary
Newly-assigned partitions show warm-path processing (no cold-path spike) in < 5s from assignment in >= 95% of cases during canary
Feature flag exists and allows enabling affinity per-cluster; rollback returns to previous consumer group behavior with zero data loss
Automated end-to-end smoke test validates ordering and at-least-once semantics for a synthetic tenant workload
tasks: Design: finalise consistent-hash vnode sizing and affinity key (tenant_id + logical-shard)
Prototype: affinity coordinator service (gRPC + lightweight consensus using lease TTLs)
Client: implement sticky lease logic in consumer library with passive handoff flow
Cache: add background cache warmer + streaming replay to populate KV/prefix caches
Infra: add feature-flag gating in control plane and per-cluster rollout API
Testing: build staging replay job and synthetic churn scenarios for validation
Observability: dashboards for rebalance count, handoff latency, % cold-path, consumer lag
Rollout: canary plan, gradual percent-based enablement, and rollback runbook
